text:
jess: Heads-up — after last night's SCIM deprov job a handful of users still show active role bindings. Logs show KMS decrypt errors when processing external_id. Anyone seen this pattern?

owen: Which job run/time?

jess: job run 2024-10-12T03:12Z. Root log snippet:
```
2024-10-12T03:12:15Z ERROR scim-provisioner: decryptExternalId failed: AccessDeniedException: User: arn:aws:sts::123456789012:assumed-role/scim-provisioner/i-abcde is not authorized to use kms:key/abcd-1234
```

liyah: hmm our SCIM service principal uses key alias `alias/redwood-scim`. Did we rotate that key last week? @idp-bot any metadata/key rotation events?

idp-bot: system: idp-metadata rotation completed 2024-10-11T22:59Z for IdP acme-sso 

oncall-sre: We did rotate a key. Audit shows key policy tightened to only allow specific IAM principals and we accidentally omitted the SCIM Lambda role. Immediate fix: add a grant or update the key policy. I'll post commands.

oncall-sre: Quick temporary fix (create a grant):
```
aws kms create-grant --key-id alias/redwood-scim --grantee-principal arn:aws:iam::123456789012:role/scim-provisioner --operations Decrypt
```

owen: Will that let us reprocess the existing queue items and finish deprovision?

oncall-sre: Yes — once the grant exists the provisioner can decrypt external_id and continue. For already-encrypted audit objects in S3 (if they were encrypted under the rotated key/material) we may need to re-encrypt or add temporary decrypt permission to the older key.

jess: Important: we store the external_id pointer in audit logs encrypted with the same KMS key. If we can't decrypt those logs compliance can't verify deprovision. Need a mitigation plan.

liyah: Proposed plan:
- add the grant so SCIM can resume ASAP
- re-run SCIM deprov for affected user batch
- for S3 audit objects: either use `aws kms re-encrypt` to move to `alias/redwood-audit` or temporarily widen old key policy for decryption during re-encrypt
- notify CS/legal if any customer records are affected

cs-tilly: Triage note: I have 3 customers already flagged by monitoring. Please ping me before changing key policies that might affect their access; we need to preserve audit trail and communications.

owen: Who has permission to run S3 re-encrypt ops? Need to ensure actions are audited and we record which principal ran it. @oncall-sre can you run re-encrypt and include the command?

oncall-sre: Example re-encrypt flow (do during maintenance window):
```
# download object, re-encrypt with destination key, upload back
aws s3 cp s3://redwood-audit/2024/10/12/part-0001.enc - | \
  aws kms re-encrypt --ciphertext-blob fileb:///dev/stdin --destination-key-id alias/redwood-audit --query CiphertextBlob --output text | base64 --decode > /tmp/part-0001.reenc
aws s3 cp /tmp/part-0001.reenc s3://redwood-audit/2024/10/12/part-0001.enc --metadata-directive REPLACE
```

oncall-sre: We'll run a small canary on 10 objects first and validate decryption and signatures. I'll open a ticket for IAM/key-policy approvals.

jess: Also, we should add an alert rule: if KMS returns AccessDenied for the `scim-provisioner` principal more than 3 times in 5m, fire a PagerDuty and post to #eng-security.

liyah: After fix: add an automated CI test that simulates key-policy tightening and fails if SCIM flows would break silently.

idp-bot: system: incident created #INC-2024-1234 (https://redwood/internal/incidents/INC-2024-1234)

owen: I'll coordinate the reprocess and mark affected customers in the incident.

jess: Opening a short runbook in the ticket with steps we discussed. Will update when deprov re-run completes. Thanks all :thumbsup:
